title: SASSA Payment Methods — Bank Transfer, Cash Send, Post Office, and Mobile Pay Points
description: Complete guide to all SASSA payment methods: bank EFT, Cash Send retail collection, Post Office collection, and mobile pay points for rural areas. How each method works and how to choose.

seo.metaTitle: SASSA Payment Methods — Bank EFT, Cash Send, Post Office & Mobile Pay Points
seo.metaDescription: Complete guide to SASSA payment methods: direct bank EFT transfer, Cash Send retail collection at Pick n Pay/Shoprite/Boxer, Post Office collection, and mobile pay points for rural beneficiaries.

contentBlocks.text: SASSA offers several ways to receive your social grant. You can choose the method that works best for your situation. You do not need a bank account to receive your grant.

This guide is for all SASSA beneficiaries who want to understand the different ways they can receive their grant payments — whether through bank transfer, Cash Send retail collection, Post Office, or mobile pay points.

SASSA deposits your grant directly into your personal South African bank account. Processing takes 1-3 business days after the official pay date. Your bank account must be registered in your own name and match your ID number exactly.

If you do not have a bank account, SASSA sends a cash voucher via SMS. Take the SMS and your ID to any participating retailer (Pick n Pay, Boxer, Shoprite, Checkers, Usave) to collect your grant in cash.
Some beneficiaries collect their grants at designated South African Post Office branches. This option is being phased out in favour of bank transfers and retail collection.
In remote rural areas, SASSA operates mobile pay points on scheduled dates. Check your local SASSA office or province hub for the monthly schedule.
Log into the SRD portal at srd.sassa.gov.za, go to 'Payment Method', and select your preferred option. Changes take effect from the following month.
